From These Lands: Mapping US Natural and Cultural Heritage at the Smithsonian

📅 2026-08-18 ✍️ Lain Graham, Esri 🏷️ Esri, Smithsonian, GIS, interactive maps, paleogeographic maps, natural heritage, cultural heritage, cartography
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

The Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History uses five animated GIS map layers to trace how biomes, migrations, and geology move across the United States in an exhibit marking the nation's 250th birthday.

📌 Key takeaways

  • The exhibit "From These Lands" at the Smithsonian marks the US 250th birthday with 600+ specimens from all 50 states and 5 territories
  • Geography, not alphabetical state-by-state listing, is the exhibit's organizing principle
  • Five animated map layers trace biomes, migrations, and geology across the country in 60-second sequences
  • Paleogeographic maps reveal how a shallow sea once split the middle of what is now the US
  • Interactive map stations let visitors send digital postcards and find natural history tied to their home states
  • The exhibit uses maps to show connections across regions, illustrating how heritage is shared across the country
